# **1\. Implementation Directive**

Implement the NPC Authoring Studio as an additive subsystem over the current ImmersiveNPCs / Orbis repository. It replaces neither Orbis cognition nor Hytale runtime authority. It turns the existing NPC Profile into a complete, server-authoritative authoring workspace for profile canon, appearance, voice samples, inventory, equipment, and live statistics.

Codex must begin by auditing the current repository revision. Names such as NpcProfilePage, CustomInventoryTransactionBridge, NpcInventoryRepository, NativeNpcInventoryController, CharacterPreviewComponent, ContextProfileBuilder, CanonicalSpeechLedger, and OrbisResourceScheduler are architectural references derived from the current project history. Reuse the current owner when it exists, rename only through deliberate refactoring, and do not re-create equivalent services under new names.

## **1.1 Required project reading**

* **Orbis Conversational Pipeline Hardening Matrix.** Preserve its one-owner-per-boundary discipline, canonical speech ownership, failure containment, and regression requirements. \[P1\]  
* **Orbis Epistemic Cognition Technical Design.** Preserve the separation between reality, belief, speech, authored canon, and inference. \[P2\]  
* **Orbis Direct Voice designs.** Reuse established voice capture, floor ownership, resource scheduling, cancellation, and speech safety boundaries. \[P3, P4\]  
* **Autonomous Evaluation Harness and Model Distillation design.** Use existing evaluation and generated-data provenance rules rather than treating generated authoring content as truth. \[P5, P6\]  
* **NPC inventory investigations R095-R119.** Preserve the proven server-authoritative Custom UI bridge, native ItemContainer authority, stable identity checks, and documented client synchronization limitations. \[P7-P11\]

## **1.2 Implementation discipline**

* **One authority per concern.** The UI may render, collect intent, and hold drafts. It may not become a second profile store, inventory, equipment store, skin format, voice repository, stat calculator, or Orbis truth source.  
* **Current-build verification.** Hytale APIs and client behavior are version-sensitive. Reconcile this design against the exact installed server/client build before coding. Record build identity and any deviation from the cited API surface.  
* **Bounded stages.** Implement adjacent stages in one Codex repository session only when each stage retains a separate automated gate, connected gate, rollback artifact, and explicit stop condition.  
* **No invisible promotion.** Generated biography, appearance drafts, and voice drafts are never authoritative until the creator explicitly saves the owning domain.  
* **No manual inventory copying.** Inventory and gear mutation must remain native ItemContainer/InventoryUtils operations. UI snapshots are derived views, not transferable state.  
* **No blocking callbacks.** Voice, UI, packet, world, and model callbacks have different threading constraints. Expensive work must leave the callback immediately and execute in a bounded worker pipeline.  
* **Preserve rollback.** The current working NPC Profile and native inventory fallback remain available until the complete studio passes all domain-specific gates.

| DEPLOYMENT GATE. A visually complete studio is not production-ready. Each domain must pass authoritative-state, stale-session, persistence, restart, connected Hytale, and rollback tests before its controls are advertised as active. |
| :---- |

# **2\. Executive Decision and Feasibility**

Decision: build a custom server-driven NPC Authoring Studio around Hytale's exposed Custom UI, inventory, cosmetics, voice, and entity-stat APIs. Do not attempt to commandeer the native My Avatar controller or embed the native Page.Bench hierarchy into the Custom UI. The project has already proved that Page.Bench owns reliable native inventory behavior, that Page.Bench exposes no usable Anchor UI target in the inspected client revision, and that the one-page Custom UI requires a server-authoritative transaction bridge and explicit UI reconciliation. \[P8-P11\]

The architecture is technically feasible because the current server API exposes an interactive Custom UI page with typed data events, inventory section resolution and native moves, inbound player voice interception, custom voice streams, a PlayerSkin protocol model, entity-stat access, and armor-slot metadata. The exact cosmetics registry methods and preview integration must still be verified against the installed build before implementation. \[H1-H10\]

| Domain | Feasibility | Primary authority | Principal uncertainty |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Workspace shell | High | InteractiveCustomUIPage and packaged Custom UI assets | Responsive composition across UI scale and resolution |
| Inventory | Proven foundation | Live Player Storage, live NPC ECS Storage, InventoryUtils | Complete merge/split/swap/quick-move matrix and cursor reconciliation |
| Gear/loadout | High with staged validation | NPC armor/loadout containers and item metadata | Exact offhand and ammunition compatibility semantics |
| Profile editor | High | Existing profile repository and schema | Unknown-field preservation and revision conflict UX |
| Generated profile assistance | High | Existing Orbis model/provider and resource scheduler | Quality, latency, and strict proposal-to-canon separation |
| Appearance editor | High for custom editor | CosmeticRegistry, PlayerSkin, CosmeticsModule, existing preview | Thumbnail availability and exact server-side registry exposure |
| Voice recorder | Moderate to high | VoiceModule interception, existing Orbis audio stack, voice asset repository | Reliable private capture/playback and capture-vs-conversation arbitration |
| Live stats | High | EntityStatMap and current combat/stat owners | Mapping a stable player-facing Defense value without recomputation |

## **2.1 Why a dedicated architecture is justified**

The Authoring Studio crosses client presentation, server-authoritative ECS state, filesystem persistence, model generation, audio capture, and long-lived NPC identity. Treating these features as unrelated buttons would create duplicate stores, stale previews, unsafe file writes, and events capable of mutating the wrong NPC. A shared session, revision model, event envelope, domain commit protocol, and connected release matrix are therefore architectural requirements rather than polish.

## **2.2 Supported outcome**

A creator should be able to create or update a sophisticated NPC entirely in game: author and generate profile content, construct a validated appearance from Hytale cosmetics, record Chatterbox reference samples, move and equip items, verify live defensive statistics, save each draft explicitly, restart the server, and then converse with the NPC through Orbis using the resulting profile and voice.

## **2.3 Explicitly unsupported assumptions**

* The native My Avatar page is not assumed to be server-callable or redirectable to a non-player target.  
* Native client panel names are not assumed to be Anchor UI keys.  
* Custom UI ItemGrid is not assumed to reconcile native drag state automatically.  
* A cosmetic asset is not assumed to expose a ready-made thumbnail.  
* A displayed stat is not assumed to exist merely because the player HUD contains a similar label.  
* A voice interceptor is not assumed to provide decoded PCM or a durable frame object.  
* A model-generated biography is not assumed to be true, safe, or canon.

# **3\. Product Definition and User Journeys**

The NPC Authoring Studio is the creator-facing product shell for ImmersiveNPCs. The existing NPC Profile becomes the overview workspace, while Profile Editor, NPC Appearance, and Voice Recorder become contextual editors that open within the same Custom UI page. Gear, stats, and both inventories remain visible as the main operational surface unless a contextual editor temporarily covers or docks beside them.

![Concept rendering of the Orbis NPC Authoring Studio with gear, profile, inventories, appearance editor, profile editor, and voice recorder.][image1]

**Figure 1\. Non-normative concept rendering approved as visual direction. Written geometry, square-slot rules, single-context-editor behavior, and authority contracts in this document take precedence.**

## **3.1 Create-new-NPC journey**

1. Creator runs /npc create \[name\].  
2. The system creates a stable NPC identity and an incomplete authoring session, not a fully valid production profile.  
3. The workspace opens with Gear/Stats, Profile Summary, and coupled inventories. Missing domains are clearly marked.  
4. Creator opens Profile Editor, enters identity and character qualities, optionally selects Generate, reviews the proposed patch, edits it, and chooses Save Profile.  
5. Creator opens NPC Appearance, chooses cosmetics and colors against a draft preview, then chooses Save Appearance.  
6. Creator opens Voice Recorder, records Reference and any optional emotional samples, privately plays them back, and saves accepted samples.  
7. Creator assigns equipment and inventory through authoritative item transactions.  
8. Creator presses the final Enter/Create action only after required domain validity checks pass.  
9. The NPC becomes spawnable/active under the existing Orbis profile lifecycle.

## **3.2 Update-existing-NPC journey**

10. Creator runs /npc update \[name\].  
11. The studio resolves the exact profile, stable ID, live entity when present, and current revisions for profile, appearance, voice, inventory, and gear.  
12. Immediate domains such as inventory and equipment transact against live authoritative containers.  
13. Draft domains such as profile and appearance remain isolated until their explicit Save actions.  
14. Closing a dirty contextual editor prompts Save, Discard, or Stay. Closing the entire studio never silently saves drafts.  
15. The session performs terminal persistence flushes, releases preview/capture leases, invalidates generations, and restores viewer state.

## **3.3 Player-facing mental model**

The creator should perceive one coherent workshop rather than a file browser. The interface should explain what can be edited, show current validity and readiness, and make ownership obvious. It should not expose implementation details such as Nemotron, PlayerSkin class names, InventorySectionId values, or technical rejection enums in normal mode.

# **4\. Scope, Goals, and Non-Goals**

## **4.1 Goals**

* Provide complete in-game authoring of an NPC's profile, appearance, voice samples, equipment, inventory, and key live stats.  
* Preserve all existing Orbis truth, cognition, memory, action, and speech ownership.  
* Reuse Hytale-native data models and transaction APIs wherever current server APIs expose them.  
* Keep generated text as an auditable proposal until explicit human save.  
* Keep profile, appearance, and voice edits draft-based, revisioned, and atomic.  
* Keep inventory and gear immediate, authoritative, replay-protected transactions.  
* Eliminate routine dependence on manual JSON editing, player-avatar export, third-party audio recording, and manual file movement.  
* Support future world systems such as Kingdoms, roles, schedules, factions, and new Core types without making the authoring UI their authority.

## **4.2 Non-goals for version 1**

* User-draggable floating panels. Panels may look independent but remain layout-managed unless a supported drag contract is proven.  
* Collaborative simultaneous editing of the same NPC. Version 1 uses one writer lease per NPC.  
* A general-purpose JSON editor.  
* A full digital audio workstation, denoiser, or waveform editor.  
* Automatic model-generated canon without creator approval.  
* Runtime model training or distillation.  
* Client-side modifications or replacement of Hytale's native My Avatar page.  
* Cross-server profile editing without a future distributed lock and shared persistence authority.  
* Arbitrary custom cosmetic creation. The first version selects from the current Hytale cosmetic catalog.  
* Inventing defensive or resistance values not present in authoritative Hytale/Orbis state.

## **4.3 Deferred opportunities**

* Template NPCs, clone-from-profile, and archetype presets.  
* Nemotron-assisted appearance constraints, such as selecting a weathered elderly blacksmith appearance from semantic criteria.  
* Batch voice recording scripts and quality coaching.  
* Relationship graph editing and visual faction membership tools.  
* Role-specific authoring extensions for guards, hunters, tavern staff, miscreants, kingdoms, schedules, shops, and quests.  
* Collaborative editing with domain-specific leases.  
* Server-hosted profile marketplace or import/export bundles, subject to asset and voice rights.

# **5\. Architectural Principles and Hard Invariants**

| Invariant | Normative rule | Failure prevented |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| UI is not authority | Every display is derived from a domain owner or an explicit draft. UI snapshots never become server truth. | Desync, item duplication, stale profile writes |
| Stable identity before names | All mutations bind to stable NPC ID plus current entity/storage identity. Display names are never sole keys. | Wrong-NPC mutation and rename drift |
| One active contextual editor | Profile, Appearance, and Voice editors are mutually exclusive within a session. | Overlapping drafts and ambiguous save actions |
| Explicit draft promotion | Profile, appearance, generated text, and recorded samples require domain-specific Save. | Silent canon or file mutation |
| Immediate item transactions | Inventory and gear use native ItemContainer/InventoryUtils transactions and authoritative rereads. | Copy/delete races and item loss |
| Revision conflict detection | Draft save compares captured base revision/hash against current authority. | Last-write-wins corruption |
| Generated text is a proposal | Generate cannot directly write profile, memory, beliefs, relationships, world state, or speech ledger. | Hallucinated canon and provenance loss |
| Voice callback remains non-blocking | Copy bounded opaque frame data, enqueue, and return. Decode and I/O run elsewhere. | Voice stalls and shared executor starvation |
| Asynchronous results are generation-bound | Late model, preview, catalog, and audio results are rejected after session/editor generation changes. | Stale preview or save |
| Atomic filesystem commits | Temporary file, validation, atomic replace, rollback copy, and post-commit hash. | Partial JSON/WAV/skin files |
| Connected evidence outranks static optimism | Client interaction, microphone behavior, preview restoration, and item movement require connected Hytale validation. | False green gates |

## **5.1 Orbis cognition invariants**

* Hytale owns reality. The studio may author canon but may not fabricate current world state. \[P2\]  
* Speech is not truth. A generated biography or recorder playback is not conversation evidence. \[P2\]  
* Authored profile data becomes evidence only through the existing profile/canon ingestion path after successful save.  
* The same mind drives dialogue and autonomy. The studio changes authoritative inputs, not a separate NPC persona used only by the UI.  
* The model is replaceable; the authored NPC state is not. Provider changes must not alter saved identity, profile, appearance, inventory, gear, or voice ownership.

## **5.2 Editor invariants**

* Cancel restores or retains the last authoritative version, never an intermediate generated or preview state.  
* Reset means restore the current persisted domain, not erase the domain to defaults.  
* Delete requires domain-specific confirmation when it can invalidate an NPC, especially deleting the Reference voice sample.  
* Technical diagnostics remain available in traces and developer mode, but player-facing messages are localized and actionable.  
* The footer advertises only controls that are actually enabled in the current feature stage.

# **6\. Existing Orbis/Hytale Ownership and Integration Boundary**

Codex must map the current code before implementation. The ownership table below describes the intended boundary, not permission to replace current production classes. Where the repository already has an equivalent owner, extend that owner or add a narrow adapter.

| Concern | Current/required owner | Authoring Studio responsibility | Forbidden replacement |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| NPC identity/profile | Existing profile and stable-ID repository | Resolve, draft, validate, atomically patch exposed fields | Name-keyed alternate profile store |
| Reality/perception | Hytale ECS and Orbis perception | Read only for status/preview where needed | Editor-authored current-world facts |
| Beliefs/memory/relationships | Epistemic core and persistence | No direct mutation in v1 except through future explicit domain tools | Free-text biography automatically becoming memory |
| Prompt rendering | Existing ContextProfileBuilder/provider path | Dedicated authoring-generation contract only | Second conversation prompt builder |
| Delivered speech | CanonicalSpeechLedger and voice delivery | Recorder playback kept private and excluded | Treating playback as canonical NPC speech |
| Model scheduling | Existing Orbis resource scheduler/provider | Low-priority cancellable Generate requests | Independent unmanaged model process |
| NPC storage | Live NPC InventoryComponent.Storage \+ NpcInventoryRepository | Display, validate intent, call native transactions, refresh | Temporary production mirror |
| Armor/loadout | Existing NPC equipment/loadout authority | Typed transaction endpoints and preview refresh | UI-only equipped state |
| Appearance | Existing skin JSON \+ Hytale PlayerSkin/cosmetics path | Draft, validate, preview, atomic save | New proprietary appearance schema |
| Voice samples | Existing voice profile/sample repository and Chatterbox cache | Capture, validate, atomic save/delete, rescan | Parallel sample naming/cache system |
| Live stats | Hytale EntityStatMap/combat systems | Build immutable snapshot for display | Local arithmetic approximation |

## **6.1 Inventory research already settled**

The project has established that section IDs and native containers are structurally correct, that Page.Bench provides reliable native transaction ownership, that Custom UI ItemGrid can expose trustworthy source and destination intent, and that explicit server-authoritative bridging is required to reconcile the one-page Custom UI. R118 and R119 therefore form the production baseline for future inventory and gear work. \[P7-P11\]

* Player Storage uses the current built-in storage section ID.  
* NPC storage is the exact live ECS Storage container, not a copied SimpleItemContainer.  
* Client-supplied item quantity is diagnostic only; the server rereads the source stack.  
* The sole ordinary mutation path is InventoryUtils or the relevant native container transaction API.  
* Both source and destination are reread after mutation and complete UI slot arrays are refreshed from authority.  
* Stable profile, entity, storage-object, session, page, and window identities are validated before mutation.  
* Raw enum messages such as AUTHORITATIVE\_SOURCE\_EMPTY are not suitable for the production UI.

## **6.2 Preview lifecycle already settled**

The studio must preserve the validated NPC preview sequence and viewer restoration contract. Opening a contextual editor may change the draft preview, but it must not mutate the logged-in player's authoritative skin or equipment. Closing, cancellation, page replacement, and reconnect must reject late preview updates and restore the viewer exactly.

## **6.3 Voice ownership already settled**

The recorder is not a new conversational channel. It must lease the existing microphone capture authority, prevent recorded speech from reaching Moonshine and the NPC conversation pipeline, and perform all expensive decode/write work outside the voice callback. The Direct Voice architecture remains authoritative for ordinary conversation. \[P3, P4\]

# **7\. High-Level Architecture**

![High-level architecture diagram showing the Interactive Custom UI page, authoring domain services, and authoritative persistence/runtime owners.][image2]

**Figure 2\. High-level Authoring Studio architecture. The page coordinates domain services; authoritative state remains in existing repositories, ECS components, and Orbis services.**

## **7.1 Layer model**

| Layer | Responsibilities | May mutate |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Presentation | Floating panels, grids, fields, buttons, tooltips, status, draft preview, waveform | No authoritative domain directly |
| Session/controller | Session IDs, editor selection, writer lease, page generation, dirty state, event decoding | Session-local state only |
| Draft services | Profile draft, appearance draft, voice recording draft, generated proposal | Draft state only |
| Domain services | Validation, catalog lookup, inventory/gear policies, stat snapshots, audio finalization | Only through owning repository/API |
| Authority adapters | Profile repository, NpcInventoryRepository, CosmeticsModule/PlayerSkin adapter, voice asset repository, EntityStatMap | Their own domain |
| Orbis integration | Authoring generation, canon ingestion, cache invalidation, resource scheduling, evaluation hooks | Only through existing Orbis owners |

## **7.2 Proposed top-level components**

* **NpcAuthoringStudioPage.** InteractiveCustomUIPage shell and central event dispatcher.  
* **NpcAuthoringSessionRegistry.** One active workspace per player and one writer lease per NPC.  
* **NpcAuthoringPanelManager.** Base-panel visibility, contextual-editor selection, responsive placement, and scrim.  
* **NpcProfileDraftService.** Schema-preserving draft, validation, revision conflict detection, and atomic save.  
* **NpcProfileGenerationService.** Provider-neutral, asynchronous, structured proposal generation.  
* **NpcAppearanceCatalogService.** Cached Hytale cosmetics catalog, categories, search, pagination, colors, and capabilities.  
* **NpcSkinCodecAdapter.** Explicit conversion among stored skin JSON, server cosmetics model, and protocol PlayerSkin.  
* **NpcVoiceRecordingService.** Capture lease, bounded Opus queue, worker processing, private playback, and atomic sample save.  
* **AuthoritativeItemMoveBridge.** Generalized storage, gear, split, merge/swap, and quick-move policies over native transactions.  
* **NpcStatsSnapshotService.** World-thread snapshot of authoritative live statistics.  
* **NpcAuthoringAuditLog.** Append-only operation records without raw voice data or model hidden reasoning.

## **7.3 Component communication rule**

All asynchronous components return immutable results carrying session ID, NPC stable ID, domain revision/hash, page generation, and editor generation. The page discards results that do not match the current session. Services do not retain a live Custom UI page reference after dismissal.

# **8\. Operating Modes, Trust Levels, and Draft/Commit Semantics**

The studio must separate authoring availability from production authority. A domain may be visible, read-only, editable as a draft, or immediately transactional. Do not infer mode from which controls happen to be visible.

| Mode | Meaning | Permitted behavior | Typical trigger |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| VIEW\_ONLY | Profile can be inspected but not mutated | Render persisted state, preview, validity, and diagnostics | Target NPC not spawned, permission missing, or writer lease held |
| AUTHORING\_READY | Base workspace has a valid writer session | Open contextual editors and transact enabled item domains | Profile and identity resolution succeeded |
| PROFILE\_DRAFT | Profile Editor owns a mutable draft | Edit and Generate proposal; no profile persistence until Save Profile | Profile Editor opened |
| APPEARANCE\_DRAFT | Appearance Editor owns a mutable skin draft | Select cosmetics, colors, and preview; no live/persisted skin change until save | NPC Appearance opened |
| VOICE\_DRAFT | Recorder owns a bounded unsaved recording | Record, process, privately play, delete draft, save sample | Voice Recorder opened |
| COMMITTING | A domain-specific save is in progress | Disable conflicting actions; validate revision and write atomically | Save Profile, Save Appearance, or Save Sample |
| DEGRADED | A non-critical service is unavailable | Retain manual editing and current persisted state; disable only affected feature | Model unavailable, microphone disabled, catalog refresh failed |
| CLOSING | Session is invalidating | Reject new events, cancel work, release leases, flush current authorities | Page close, disconnect, NPC delete, plugin shutdown |

## **8.1 Trust levels**

| Data class | Trust level | How it becomes authoritative |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Custom UI event payload | Untrusted intent | Never directly; validate against current session and server state |
| UI-rendered slot/field value | Presentation snapshot | Never directly; reread owning repository/container |
| Profile draft | Session-local proposed state | Save Profile after validation and revision check |
| Generated profile patch | Unverified proposal | Creator reviews/edits, then Save Profile |
| Appearance draft | Session-local proposed skin | Validate and Save Appearance |
| Voice recording draft | Unsaved media | Validate and Save Sample |
| Live ItemContainer state | Authoritative runtime item state | Already authoritative after native transaction |
| Persisted profile/skin/voice file | Authoritative durable state | Atomic domain save and successful post-write validation |
| EntityStat snapshot | Read-only authoritative snapshot | Captured from live ECS owner at one instant |

# **9\. Unified Authoring Session and Concurrency**

Every workspace open creates one NpcAuthoringSession. The session is the anti-staleness boundary joining the viewer, stable NPC identity, live entity, container/window bindings, editor drafts, preview ownership, voice capture ownership, and domain revisions. It is not a persistence store.

![Unified NPC authoring session state machine from closed through editing, committing, and closing.][image4]

**Figure 4\. Unified authoring session state machine. Contextual editors are mutually exclusive; saves pass through a committing state; closure invalidates all generations before releasing resources.**

## **9.1 Required session identity**

record NpcAuthoringSessionIdentity(  
    UUID sessionId,  
    UUID viewerPlayerId,  
    UUID npcStableId,  
    UUID npcEntityUuid,  
    long pageGeneration,  
    Instant openedAt  
) {}

* npcStableId is required even when the NPC is not currently spawned.  
* npcEntityUuid and entity Ref are required for live inventory, gear, preview, and stats transactions.  
* pageGeneration changes whenever the page instance or authoritative window set changes.  
* Each contextual editor has its own editorGeneration and captured base revision/hash.  
* A result is accepted only when every applicable identity still matches.

## **9.2 Session registry**

NpcAuthoringSessionRegistry should provide atomic open, lookup, close, and writer-lease operations. The registry must reject a second active workspace for the same player, and it must reject a second writer for the same NPC unless a future read-only collaboration mode is explicitly implemented.

| Operation | Precondition | Result | Failure behavior |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| open(viewer, npc) | Viewer has permission; no active viewer session; no NPC writer lease | Registers session and lease | Readable conflict; no partial page |
| resolve(event) | Session/page generation matches active page | Returns immutable session view | Reject and refresh or silently ignore stale event |
| switchEditor(kind) | Current editor clean or creator confirms action | Closes current draft and opens target | Save / Discard / Stay prompt |
| close(reason) | Any lifecycle path | Marks closing, invalidates generations, releases resources | Idempotent; late events fail closed |
| heartbeat/validate | Optional for long sessions | Confirms entity/window/storage identity | Degrade live domains or require reopen |

## **9.3 Writer lease**

Use one writer lease per NPC across profile, appearance, voice, inventory, and gear in version 1\. This is deliberately conservative. Inventory itself may change from gameplay while the studio is open; therefore item operations always reread live state and do not rely on the lease as a substitute for container authority. The lease protects authored files and editor intent from another authoring session, not from legitimate world simulation.

## **9.4 Revision model**

| Domain | Captured at open | Conflict check | Conflict response |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Profile | Profile revision and canonical JSON hash | Before Save Profile | Preserve draft; show Reload / Copy Draft / Cancel |
| Appearance | Skin revision and canonical skin hash | Before Save Appearance | Preserve draft; require rebase or discard |
| Voice sample | Per-emotion sample revision/hash | Before Save/Delete Sample | Do not overwrite; refresh current sample |
| Inventory | No static revision dependency | Reread source/target immediately before every move | Reject stale move and refresh grids |
| Gear/loadout | No static revision dependency | Reread source, target, filters, and live equipment immediately | Reject stale move and refresh gear/inventory |

## **9.5 Lifecycle termination**

* Page dismissal: invalidate bridge and editor generations before flushing or restoring anything.  
* Player disconnect: close session, stop capture/playback, discard drafts, unregister listeners, flush item persistence.  
* NPC unload/despawn: retain profile draft if safe, but live inventory/gear/stats become unavailable and events reject until reopen.  
* NPC deletion: abort all editors, release writer lease, prevent any late file or item mutation.  
* Plugin shutdown/world unload: stop new sessions, close active sessions in bounded time, preserve durable authorities, log incomplete cleanup.

# **10\. Custom UI Shell, Panel Manager, and Navigation**

NpcAuthoringStudioPage remains one InteractiveCustomUIPage so profile summary, preview, inventories, and contextual authoring tools share one session and one event envelope. Hytale's InteractiveCustomUIPage supports typed interactive data events; the installed build remains the authority for exact construction and page-lifetime APIs. \[H1\]

## **10.1 Base shell**

* Gear \+ Stats floating panel at upper left.  
* Profile Summary floating panel at upper right.  
* Coupled Inventory floating panel beneath both.  
* Contextual editor host capable of rendering one of Profile Editor, NPC Appearance, or Voice Recorder.  
* Optional dark scrim while a centered contextual editor is open.  
* Slim bottom input legend outside or beneath the coupled inventory panel.  
* No giant shared outer frame in the final visual composition.

## **10.2 Panel manager responsibilities**

| Responsibility | Required behavior |
| :---- | :---- |
| Composition | Build and update panel documents without replacing authoritative page/window bindings unnecessarily |
| Visibility | Show one contextual editor, base panels, scrim, status overlays, and confirmation dialogs |
| Geometry | Select a resolution/UI-scale layout profile and preserve square slots |
| Dirty navigation | Block editor switch/close until Save, Discard, or Stay is resolved |
| Event routing | Decode central event envelope and dispatch only allowed action for active editor |
| Refresh coalescing | Combine related profile, preview, inventory, gear, stats, and voice UI updates |
| Failure UX | Show localized actionable message and preserve technical reason in trace |
| Accessibility | Provide readable labels/tooltips and avoid relying on color alone for state |

## **10.3 Panel implementation boundary**

Visually floating does not imply independent Custom UI pages. The initial implementation should use separately decorated containers within the same page, placed by NpcAuthoringPanelManager. Do not implement user drag-to-reposition until the current Custom UI event model proves a reliable panel-drag contract that cannot interfere with ItemGrid interaction.

## **10.4 Contextual editor host**

At 1920 x 1080, opening a contextual editor should retain the base workspace behind a restrained scrim and place the editor in the foreground. At 2560 x 1440 and wider, the panel manager may translate the base workspace left and dock the contextual editor to the right. Only one contextual editor is active. The page, inventory windows, and preview ownership should remain stable while editors are switched.

## **10.5 Confirmation dialogs**

* Dirty contextual editor close: Save / Discard / Stay.  
* Delete saved voice sample: Delete / Cancel, with stronger warning for Reference.  
* Reset draft: Reset to persisted version / Cancel.  
* Revision conflict: Reload authority / Copy draft to clipboard or export recovery file / Cancel.  
* Discard newly created incomplete NPC: Delete incomplete profile / Keep draft profile / Cancel.

# **11\. Visual Design System and Layout Geometry**

The studio should feel native to Hytale without depending on undocumented native client asset paths. Reuse the supported Common UI style library where appropriate, and package project-authored images inside the ImmersiveNPCs asset pack. Hytale's shared Common.ui styles are intended to help Custom UI match the core game UI. \[H11\]

![Normative workspace geometry showing Gear and Stats, Profile Summary, and coupled Inventory panels.][image5]

**Figure 5\. Normative base workspace geometry. Numeric values are starting targets and must be reconciled with current UI scale; alignment and square-slot invariants are mandatory.**

![Contextual editor placement at 1920 by 1080 and 2560 by 1440 or wider.][image6]

**Figure 6\. Contextual editor placement. The first implementation manages panel position; it does not promise free user dragging.**

## **11.1 Color and semantic identity**

| Element | Semantic treatment | Guidance |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Player | Cyan/turquoise | Retain Hytale's player-associated visual language where visible |
| Neutral NPC | Gold/yellow | Use NPCBackground@2x.png behind the NPC preview; do not imply hostile red |
| Hostile/monster future extension | Crimson/red | Deferred; do not couple current studio behavior to hostility color |
| Primary action | Hytale blue | Save and Enter are strongest rightmost actions |
| Warning | Amber/yellow | Recoverable issue, incomplete requirement, or compatibility warning |
| Error | Red | Rejected mutation or invalid draft; include text, not color alone |
| Success/ready | Green | Voice ready, valid profile, successful save or rescan |

## **11.2 Panel geometry**

| Panel | 1920 x 1080 target | Alignment rule | Responsive rule |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Gear \+ Stats | x 160, y 40, w 760, h 510 | Left edge aligns with coupled inventories | Uniformly scale; keep preview and slot columns legible |
| Profile Summary | x 944, y 40, w 816, h 510 | Right edge aligns with coupled inventories | May narrow text summary before shrinking buttons |
| Coupled Inventories | x 160, y 574, w 1600, h about 370 | Spans both top panels | Keep slot aspect ratio 1:1 and preserve center rail |
| Contextual editor | Centered foreground | One editor only | Dock right only when safe width remains |
| Footer legend | Bottom safe area, about 44 high | Center under workspace | Hide unsupported controls before compressing text |

## **11.3 Square-slot invariant**

Inventory and equipment slots must remain square at every supported UI scale. Do not fit the workspace by scaling width and height independently. Use Hytale's current default ItemGrid slot size, spacing, icon scale, quantity placement, durability overlay, and padding where those styles are available to Custom UI. A layout that fits only by producing rectangular cells is rejected.

## **11.4 NPC presentation assets**

![Contact sheet of project UI assets including the gold NPC background and weapon, shield, ammo, armor, and special-slot icons.][image7]

**Figure 7\. Project assets referenced by the visual design. These files must be packaged under stable mod-relative paths; local developer installation paths are not production dependencies.**

* NPCBackground@2x.png: gold/yellow character-preview background.  
* WeaponSlotIconSword@2x.png: transparent Primary Weapon semantic overlay.  
* WeaponSlotIconShield@2x.png: transparent Shield/Offhand semantic overlay.  
* WeaponSlotIconAmmo@2x.png: transparent Preferred Ammunition semantic overlay.  
* Armor slot overlays may use compatible project-packaged copies or current mod assets, not hard references into the user's Hytale client installation.  
* SpecialSlot@2x.png is a reference for visual treatment; do not assume it is a reusable Custom UI dependency unless packaged lawfully and supported.

## **11.5 Typography and action ordering**

* Use Hytale-compatible sans-serif styling and supported Common.ui components.  
* Headers use uppercase or title case consistently within the same panel family.  
* Primary save action is rightmost and visually strongest.  
* Profile Editor bottom order is exactly: Generate | Reset | Cancel | Save Profile.  
* Appearance bottom order is: Randomize | Reset | Cancel | Save Appearance.  
* Voice Recorder controls are state-dependent; Save Sample is the final commit action.  
* Do not display provider names in creator-facing Generate controls.

# **12\. Workspace Navigation State Machine**

Navigation is an explicit state machine, not a collection of independent Visible toggles. The panel manager and session controller own the current editor kind, dirty state, confirmation state, and allowed transitions.

| From | Action | Guard | To | Side effects |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| READY | Open Profile Editor | Writer lease valid | PROFILE\_EDIT | Create profile draft and editor generation |
| READY | Open NPC Appearance | Cosmetics service available | APPEARANCE\_EDIT | Create skin draft and preview lease |
| READY | Open Voice Recorder | Voice permission and input capability | VOICE\_EDIT | Create recorder session; capture not yet active |
| Any editor clean | Open another editor | No unsaved draft | Target editor | Dispose current draft, increment editor generation |
| Any editor dirty | Open another editor | Creator chooses Save/Discard | Target editor or current | Commit or discard current draft |
| Any editor | Cancel | If dirty, confirmation | READY | Discard draft and restore authoritative preview |
| COMMITTING | Save succeeds | Revision still current | READY or same editor | Refresh summary/caches/revisions |
| COMMITTING | Save fails | Rollback complete | Same editor | Keep draft, show actionable error |
| READY/editor | Close studio | Dirty editors resolved | CLOSED | Invalidate generations, flush items, release leases |

## **12.1 Navigation rejection**

A stale event from a hidden editor, old page generation, closed recording, or prior NPC must be ignored or rejected without changing the active workspace. The page should refresh the affected controls from current state when silence would confuse the creator.

## **12.2 URL/file browser behavior**

Raw file browsing is an advanced/developer function. Opening the profile, skin, or voice folders must never replace the normal authoring workflow. If the operating system cannot open the path, show a non-fatal message and keep the studio session intact.

# **13\. NPC Gear and Stats Panel**

The Gear \+ Stats panel combines a live NPC preview, four armor slots, three loadout slots, one ammunition policy, and authoritative live statistics. Its purpose is to author and inspect the NPC's current embodied state, not merely display decorative cells.

## **13.1 Panel composition**

| Region | Content | Behavior |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Header | \[NAME\]'S GEAR or NPC GEAR | Stable title; optional validity icon |
| Left slot column | Head, Chest, Hands, Legs | Filtered equipment endpoints; eye toggle visible only when occupied |
| Center | Character preview over gold NPC background | Reflects draft appearance when Appearance Editor active, otherwise authoritative live state |
| Right slot column | Primary Weapon, Shield/Offhand, Preferred Ammo | Typed loadout endpoints and semantic overlay icons |
| Ammo policy | Infinite Ammunition checkbox \+ tooltip | Enabled only when meaningful for selected weapon |
| Stats strip | Health, Stamina, Mana, Defense | Authoritative snapshot, event/coalesced refresh |

## **13.2 Preview state priority**

16. If Appearance Editor has an active valid draft, render that draft skin in the studio preview.  
17. Otherwise render the authoritative saved NPC skin.  
18. Always overlay the current authoritative equipment/loadout unless the Appearance Editor is explicitly previewing cosmetic conflict behavior.  
19. Do not let an unsaved profile draft change physical appearance.  
20. Do not mutate the live NPC for every appearance click; apply the live NPC only after Save Appearance.  
21. After a committed gear transaction, update both live NPC equipment and studio preview through the validated equipment update path.

## **13.3 Armor visibility**

Each occupied armor slot may expose the established visibility toggle. Visibility is separate typed state and must persist independently from the item. Toggling visibility does not unequip or move the item. An empty slot has no eye control. Compatibility and visibility changes must refresh the preview without changing item ownership.

## **13.4 Loadout labels and tooltips**

* **Primary Weapon.** Current/preferred combat weapon selected from a compatible item.  
* **Shield / Offhand.** Validated shield or supported offhand item; compatibility is not determined from display names.  
* **Preferred Ammunition.** Explicit ammunition preference or actual loadout stack according to the repository's existing domain model.  
* **Infinite Ammunition.** Tooltip text: "Toggle for infinite ammunition." The checkbox is disabled when no compatible ranged weapon is selected.

## **13.5 Panel refresh triggers**

* Workspace open and live entity rebind.  
* Committed armor/loadout move.  
* Armor visibility change.  
* Saved appearance change.  
* Authoritative stat change or coalesced fallback refresh.  
* NPC unload/reload or equipment-component replacement.  
* Profile role/name change affecting labels only.

# **14\. Coupled Inventory Panel**

The inventories belong in one shared visual frame because they form one interaction surface. The left side shows the target NPC's fixed 40-slot storage; the right side shows the viewing player's actual Storage capacity. A narrow transfer rail communicates direction and may later support selected-stack quick moves.

## **14.1 Authoritative bindings**

| Surface | Authority | Capacity | Persistence |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| NPC Inventory | Exact live NPC InventoryComponent.Storage ItemContainer | 40 slots unless current domain migration says otherwise | Existing NpcInventoryRepository listener and terminal flush |
| Player Inventory | Viewing player's actual Storage ItemContainer | Current Hytale capacity | Hytale player persistence |
| Transfer rail | No item authority | Two selected-stack actions | None |

## **14.2 Initial item interactions**

* Left-click full-stack move to empty slot.  
* Internal rearrangement in both grids.  
* Compatible stack merge.  
* Occupied-slot swap where native transaction semantics support atomic swap.  
* Partial split and one-item placement matching proven Hytale semantics.  
* Quick move/shift behavior using InventoryUtils.smartMoveItem or current native equivalent.  
* Full destination and incompatible destination rejection with authoritative snapback.  
* Close while carrying or during a pending event without loss or duplication.

## **14.3 Transfer arrow rail**

The dual-arrow rail is a useful affordance but must not become a shortcut around selection and validation. In the first visual stage, show disabled buttons with tooltips. Activate only after the studio can identify one authoritative selected source stack, the destination policy is unambiguous, and the quick-move path passes the same replay, stale-state, capacity, and persistence gates as drag/drop.

* NPC-to-Player arrow: move selected NPC stack into Player Storage using current pickup/quick-move policy.  
* Player-to-NPC arrow: move selected Player stack into NPC Storage, merging only through native transaction behavior.  
* Never interpret the arrows as Take All or Put All.  
* Disable when no valid selection, wrong direction, stale session, or destination has no capacity.

## **14.4 Visual synchronization**

After every accepted or rejected operation, rebuild affected ItemGrid slot arrays from the authoritative ItemContainers. Do not patch only the cell the client claimed changed. The R116-R119 investigations showed that client presentation can remain stale even after a native transaction and UpdateWindow; the explicit bridge reconciliation remains required. \[P9-P11\]

## **14.5 Player-facing status**

| Internal reason | Player-facing text | UI behavior |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| AUTHORITATIVE\_SOURCE\_EMPTY | That item is no longer there. | Refresh both grids; no intrusive modal |
| DESTINATION\_FULL | There is no room for that item. | Refresh and retain source |
| INCOMPATIBLE\_ITEM | That item cannot be placed in this slot. | Highlight destination briefly |
| STALE\_SESSION | The inventory changed. Try again. | Refresh all item surfaces |
| NPC\_UNAVAILABLE | This NPC is no longer available. | Disable live item editing; require reopen |
| DUPLICATE\_EVENT |  | Suppress and refresh silently |

# **15\. Server-Authoritative Inventory Transaction Completion**

![Server-authoritative inventory and gear transaction pipeline from Custom UI intent through Hytale transaction, UI reconciliation, and persistence.][image8]

**Figure 8\. Server-authoritative item pipeline. UI events are intent; Hytale containers and transactions remain the sole mutation authority.**

## **15.1 Generalized bridge**

Generalize the current CustomInventoryTransactionBridge only after auditing its current production revision. Prefer a narrow policy composition over a second bridge implementation.

AuthoritativeItemMoveBridge  
  \+ StorageMovePolicy  
  \+ EquipmentMovePolicy  
  \+ LoadoutMovePolicy  
  \+ SplitMovePolicy  
  \+ MergeSwapPolicy  
  \+ QuickMovePolicy  
  \+ UiReconciliationPolicy

## **15.2 Immutable move intent**

record AuthoringItemMoveIntent(  
    UUID operationId,  
    UUID sessionId,  
    long pageGeneration,  
    UUID viewerPlayerId,  
    UUID npcStableId,  
    int sourceSectionId,  
    int sourceSlotId,  
    int targetSectionId,  
    int targetSlotId,  
    int requestedQuantityDiagnostic,  
    int mouseButton,  
    MoveGesture gesture,  
    long clientEventSequence  
) {}

The client-supplied item ID and quantity may be retained for diagnostics, but they never determine mutation. The bridge resolves the source section, rereads the authoritative source ItemStack, derives the allowed quantity from the validated gesture, and lets Hytale's transaction API enforce container filters, stack limits, and legal moves.

## **15.3 Validation order**

22. Resolve active authoring session and exact page instance.  
23. Validate viewer ownership, stable NPC ID, current entity UUID/Ref, and writer permission.  
24. Validate page generation, window registration, and exact container object identities.  
25. Allowlist source and target sections for the active domain.  
26. Validate source and target slot bounds against current capacities.  
27. Reread authoritative source and target stacks.  
28. Validate gesture, button, and quantity policy.  
29. Suppress duplicate/replayed physical releases.  
30. Execute on the required world thread.  
31. Call the current native move/smart-move/container transaction.  
32. Reread all affected containers and classify result.  
33. Refresh UI from authority and persist through existing listeners.

## **15.4 Operation semantics**

| Operation | Preferred native path | Acceptance |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Full-stack move | InventoryUtils.moveItem | Exact source removal/target addition or clean rejection |
| Internal move | InventoryUtils.moveItem | Same section allowed; same-slot becomes no-op |
| Compatible merge | InventoryUtils.moveItem/container move | Native stack limit and remainder; no local arithmetic writes |
| Occupied swap | Native atomic swap/move semantics if supported | Both items exchange or operation rejects without mutation |
| Partial split | InventoryUtils.moveItem with validated quantity | Matches connected Page.Bench behavior |
| Quick move | InventoryUtils.smartMoveItem or exact native strategy | Deterministic direction limited to Player Storage and NPC Storage |

## **15.5 Replay protection**

Custom UI may emit multiple related events for one gesture. Select one mutation trigger and treat all hover/drag-complete/cancel events as observation or reconciliation signals. A short-lived fingerprint includes session, generation, source/target section and slot, authoritative quantity, gesture, and client event sequence. Suppression must be logged without allowing delayed events to mutate a new page.

## **15.6 Post-operation convergence**

* Classify COMMITTED, REJECTED, NO\_OP, STALE, INVALID, or DUPLICATE from authoritative post-state.  
* Refresh complete source and target slot arrays, not assumed deltas.  
* Ensure drag/cursor visual state is cleared through the current proven reconciliation method.  
* Flush or queue persistence only through the existing repository listener/terminal flush.  
* Record before/after summaries and operation ID without logging sensitive metadata payloads unnecessarily.

## **15.7 Completion gate**

Storage movement is complete only after Player internal, NPC internal, bidirectional transfer, merge, swap, partial split, quick move, full destination, stale source, repeated event, close while dragging, reopen, restart, and at least 100 mixed operations pass with zero loss, duplication, ghost items, wrong-section moves, or wrong-NPC mutations.

# **16\. Gear and Loadout Transaction Architecture**

Gear is not a cosmetic overlay on storage. It is a set of authoritative equipment endpoints with stricter compatibility, displacement, preview, stat, and persistence consequences. Implement gear only after the storage bridge is production-green.

## **16.1 Endpoint graph**

Player Storage  \<-\>  NPC Armor  
NPC Storage     \<-\>  NPC Armor

Player Storage  \<-\>  NPC Loadout  
NPC Storage     \<-\>  NPC Loadout

NPC Armor       \-\>   Player or NPC Storage on unequip  
NPC Loadout     \-\>   Player or NPC Storage on unequip

Do not allow armor-to-loadout or loadout-to-armor direct moves unless a future explicit operation defines them. Every endpoint is allowlisted by the active session and the exact current container/window identities.

## **16.2 Equipment move policy**

| Stage | Rule |
| :---- | :---- |
| Intent | Dropped/quick-equip event identifies source and semantic target slot; event remains untrusted |
| Compatibility | Resolve current item asset and validate actual armor/loadout metadata against target |
| Displacement | If target occupied, use proven atomic swap/displace behavior or reject |
| Mutation | Call native container transaction; never local copy/remove/add |
| Post-state | Reread source, target, all equipment containers, and visibility state |
| Runtime application | Create/apply authoritative EquipmentUpdate and refresh live NPC/preview |
| Stats | Capture fresh authoritative stat snapshot after equipment update settles |
| Persistence | Existing equipment/inventory owner records the committed state and terminally flushes |

## **16.3 Armor slots**

* Head accepts only items whose authoritative armor slot maps to Head.  
* Chest accepts only Chest.  
* Hands accepts only Hands.  
* Legs accepts only Legs.  
* No display-name, icon, category-text, or filename heuristics are sufficient when item metadata is available.  
* Armor visibility remains attached to the semantic armor slot, not to the item's current array index.

## **16.4 Loadout slots**

* Primary Weapon accepts a compatible weapon/tool according to current item asset metadata and NPC combat capability.  
* Shield / Offhand accepts a real shield or supported offhand item. If the installed build lacks a general offhand contract, define a documented adapter based on actual item configuration.  
* Preferred Ammunition accepts or references ammunition compatible with the selected primary weapon under the existing loadout model.  
* Changing Primary Weapon must revalidate the Preferred Ammunition and Infinite Ammunition policy.  
* Invalid dependent state is not silently deleted. Keep the item authoritative and mark the configuration invalid until the creator resolves it, unless the current domain has a safer established rule.

## **16.5 Occupied targets and full inventories**

The dangerous case is equipping into an occupied target when the displaced item has nowhere to go. Before mutation, establish whether the native transaction can atomically swap or place the displaced item into the source slot. If not, reject the operation. Do not temporarily remove an item and hope a later insertion succeeds. Unequip into full storage should normally reject rather than world-drop.

## **16.6 Equipment update ordering**

34. Commit native container transaction.  
35. Reread equipment and storage authorities.  
36. Persist/queue the domain change through existing owner.  
37. Build EquipmentUpdate from authoritative equipment containers using current Hytale API.  
38. Apply to live NPC on the world thread.  
39. Update studio preview using its existing validated preview/restoration sequence.  
40. Capture and publish a fresh stats snapshot.  
41. Refresh gear cells, inventory cells, visibility buttons, compatibility indicators, and footer controls in one coalesced UI update.

## **16.7 Failure behavior**

* Incompatible item: reject, refresh, and show readable slot-specific message.  
* NPC entity changed/unloaded: reject all live gear moves and require reopen.  
* Preview update failed after committed equipment move: keep authoritative equipment, mark preview degraded, and retry/rebuild preview without rolling back the item transaction unless the domain contract explicitly requires coupled atomicity.  
* Persistence flush failed: retain live authoritative state, surface critical save error, prevent session close from claiming success, and preserve retry/rollback evidence.

# **17\. Equipment Compatibility and Ammunition Semantics**

Compatibility must be derived from current item configuration, not assumptions. The Hytale protocol and server asset model expose armor-slot and resistance/stat metadata; the current installed build must be inspected for weapon, projectile, shield/offhand, and ammunition relationships. \[H10\]

## **17.1 Compatibility resolver**

interface NpcEquipmentCompatibilityResolver {  
    CompatibilityVerdict validateArmor(Item item, ArmorSlot target);  
    CompatibilityVerdict validatePrimaryWeapon(Item item, NpcCapabilitySnapshot npc);  
    CompatibilityVerdict validateOffhand(Item item, Item primaryWeapon, NpcCapabilitySnapshot npc);  
    CompatibilityVerdict validateAmmunition(Item ammo, Item primaryWeapon);  
}

Each verdict should contain a typed reason, evidence describing the item configuration inspected, and whether the conclusion is authoritative, unsupported, or requires review. Avoid silently treating UNKNOWN as compatible.

## **17.2 Primary Weapon**

* Use the item asset's actual weapon/tool configuration and interaction capabilities.  
* Validate the NPC has or can receive the required combat capability/animation contract.  
* Do not accept arbitrary blocks or consumables because Hytale can render them in hand.  
* Do not assume all spears, bows, crossbows, staves, or daggers share identical ammunition/offhand behavior.

## **17.3 Shield and offhand**

The player's native UI visually presents a special shield/offhand region, but a native visual slot is not itself a server-side compatibility rule. Codex must trace current item and interaction metadata. If only shields are reliably classified, version 1 should call the endpoint Shield / Offhand but enable shields first and mark other offhand categories unsupported rather than guessing.

## **17.4 Preferred ammunition model**

Before implementation, inspect the existing NpcInventoryState and loadout persistence. Choose one authoritative model:

| Model | Meaning | Rule |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Physical loadout stack | Ammo slot owns a real ItemStack consumed during combat | Moving ammo to the slot changes item ownership; no duplicate copy remains in storage |
| Preference pointer | Ammo slot stores an item-type preference while physical ammo remains in storage | UI clearly distinguishes preference from stack quantity; combat selects matching storage stack |

Do not combine the two models. If Hytale's own ranged weapons draw from backpack/storage and do not expose a public multi-ammo priority, the Orbis Preferred Ammunition selection should be explicit and deterministic. If no preference is set, use a documented fallback discovered from the current build or refuse to infer an arbitrary priority.

## **17.5 Infinite Ammunition**

* Infinite Ammunition is a policy flag, not a hidden stack generator.  
* Combat authorization checks the policy only after validating a compatible primary weapon and preferred ammunition.  
* The setting must not affect Player inventory or ordinary item transfer.  
* The UI disables the setting when the loadout cannot use ammunition and shows why.  
* Server operators should be able to permission-gate or globally disable the policy in balance-sensitive environments.

## **17.6 Compatibility invalidation**

When a dependency changes, revalidate in this order: Primary Weapon, Offhand, Preferred Ammunition, Infinite Ammunition. An invalid dependent selection should be marked and prevented from gameplay use. Do not silently delete or transfer the item as a side effect of selecting a different weapon.

# **18\. Live Stats Snapshot and Refresh**

The Gear panel shows live defensive context so the creator can verify that equipment actually affects the NPC. The values must be captured from current Hytale ECS/stat/combat owners. EntityStatMap exposes live stat values; exact stat IDs and aggregate defense ownership must be audited in the installed build. \[H9\]

## **18.1 Stats snapshot contract**

record NpcStatsSnapshot(  
    UUID npcStableId,  
    UUID npcEntityUuid,  
    Instant capturedAt,  
    Optional\<StatValue\> health,  
    Optional\<StatValue\> stamina,  
    Optional\<StatValue\> mana,  
    Optional\<DefenseSnapshot\> defense,  
    Map\<String, ResistanceValue\> optionalResistances,  
    long equipmentRevision  
) {}

## **18.2 Display rules**

* Health shows current / maximum when both are authoritative.  
* Stamina and Mana are hidden or marked unavailable when the NPC lacks those stats; do not display fabricated 0/0.  
* Defense shows the current authoritative aggregate or a clearly labeled base resistance/stat if no aggregate exists.  
* Detailed resistances may be exposed in a tooltip or future expanded panel only when actual damage-class data is available.  
* A snapshot includes capture time and equipment revision so stale values can be recognized.

## **18.3 Refresh strategy**

42. Capture on workspace open after live entity/equipment binding succeeds.  
43. Capture after committed gear transaction and resulting equipment application.  
44. Subscribe to an authoritative stat/equipment change signal when current APIs expose one.  
45. Otherwise use a low-frequency coalesced refresh while the Gear panel is visible.  
46. Never poll every frame and never perform expensive traversal from the UI callback.  
47. Reject snapshot results whose entity UUID, equipment revision, session, or page generation no longer matches.

## **18.4 Failure behavior**

If stats cannot be read, inventory and profile authoring should remain available. The panel shows an unavailable state and logs the exact missing stat or component. Do not treat a missing optional stat as an invalid NPC unless an existing gameplay contract requires it.

# **19\. NPC Profile Summary Panel**

The Profile Summary panel is the compact overview and navigation surface. It should answer whether the NPC is valid and ready, expose the three authoring entry points, and keep raw file operations secondary.

## **19.1 Summary fields**

| Field | Source | Display rule |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Name | Authoritative profile | Primary panel identity |
| Role / occupation | Authoritative profile | One concise line; hide when absent |
| Biography summary | Authoritative profile | One or two lines with ellipsis; full text lives in Profile Editor |
| Profile status | Profile validator | Ready, Incomplete, Invalid, or Read-only |
| Appearance status | Skin validator / live binding | Ready, Missing, Invalid, or Draft |
| Voice status | Voice profile scanner | Reference ready plus emotional-sample summary |
| Inventory / gear status | Live binding and persistence health | Normal, Read-only, Save error, or NPC unavailable |

## **19.2 Primary actions**

* **Profile Editor.** Opens the structured profile authoring window.  
* **NPC Appearance.** Opens the Hytale-cosmetics-backed appearance editor.  
* **Voice Recorder.** Opens the in-game sample recording and playback window.

## **19.3 Advanced actions**

Existing Open, Browse, Rescan, and file-location controls may remain in a collapsed Advanced/Developer section. The normal creator workflow must not require Windows Explorer. Any advanced file action must remain permission-gated, path-contained, non-fatal, and unable to invalidate the active session if the operating system action fails.

## **19.4 Status refresh**

Refresh the summary after each successful domain save, voice rescan, inventory persistence failure/recovery, NPC rebind, and validation result. Do not rebuild the entire studio merely to update one status line; use a coalesced summary patch.

# **20\. Profile Editor Domain Model**

Profile Editor exposes meaningful authored concepts rather than raw JSON. It operates on an NpcProfileDraft cloned from the current authoritative profile. The draft retains stable identity, base revision/hash, field-level dirtiness, validation results, generated proposal provenance, and unknown extension data.

## **20.1 Draft contract**

record NpcProfileDraft(  
    UUID draftId,  
    UUID sessionId,  
    UUID npcStableId,  
    long baseProfileRevision,  
    String baseCanonicalHash,  
    NpcProfileEditableFields fields,  
    Set\<ProfileFieldPath\> dirtyFields,  
    Map\<String, JsonNode\> preservedExtensions,  
    Optional\<GeneratedProfileProposal\> proposal,  
    ProfileValidationReport validation,  
    long editorGeneration  
) {}

## **20.2 Editable field groups**

| Group | Example fields | Authority notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Identity | Display name, title, species/race, age, pronouns, role, occupation, home/base, faction/community IDs | Stable NPC ID is immutable and never edited as display text |
| Personality | Traits, values, likes, dislikes, fears, boundaries, temperament, moral outlook, work ethic | Stored in existing profile schema or explicit schema extension |
| Biography | Short summary, full background, major life events, current circumstances | Authored canon after Save Profile |
| Motivations | Goals, desires, ambitions, obligations, personal stakes | Must map cleanly to existing self-model/profile ingestion |
| Behavior and speech | Speech style, vocabulary, mannerisms, social preferences, expertise, avoided topics, creator instructions | Does not bypass Epistemic claim authorization |
| Relationships | Stable target IDs, relationship type, authored history/starting state where supported | Reuse existing relationship authority; read-only until safe editor exists |
| Advanced | Schema version, optional extension fields, provenance, developer notes | Permission-gated; no raw arbitrary file paths |

## **20.3 Schema ownership**

Codex must inspect the current profile schema and map each editor field to an existing typed field before adding new keys. If a required concept is not represented, add a versioned schema extension and migration rather than storing an unstructured duplicate. Do not create fields that conflict with belief, memory, relationship, task, or world-state ownership.

## **20.4 Stable identity**

* npcStableId cannot be edited in Profile Editor.  
* Display name may change without changing stable identity.  
* Relationships and references use stable IDs with readable display names.  
* A profile rename updates file/display conventions only through the existing safe rename path; it must not orphan memory, inventory, voice, skin, or relationships.

## **20.5 Validation categories**

| Severity | Meaning | Save behavior |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| INFO | Suggestion or optional completeness note | Save allowed |
| WARNING | Potentially weak authoring, missing optional sample, or unresolved reference | Save allowed after clear warning where appropriate |
| ERROR | Schema invalid, required identity missing, illegal ID/reference, length violation, or incompatible field combination | Save blocked |
| CONFLICT | Base revision/hash changed since draft open | Save blocked; offer rebase/reload |

# **21\. Profile Editor UX, Validation, and Unknown-Field Preservation**

The editor should resemble a structured game tool, not a database form. Use category navigation, concise labels, multiline fields where appropriate, inline validation, and a persistent bottom action row.

## **21.1 Window layout**

| Region | Content |
| :---- | :---- |
| Header | PROFILE EDITOR \- \[NAME\], close button, dirty indicator |
| Left category rail | Identity, Personality, Biography, Behavior & Speech, Relationships, Advanced |
| Main form | Only fields for the selected category; scrollable when necessary |
| Generation scope | Optional selector for Biography, Personality, Motivations, Speech, or All Allowed Fields |
| Validation strip | Inline errors/warnings and generated-proposal status |
| Bottom actions | Generate | Reset | Cancel | Save Profile |

## **21.2 Button semantics**

| Action | Exact semantics |
| :---- | :---- |
| Generate | Create a structured proposal from the current draft. Do not save, close, or overwrite protected fields. |
| Reset | Restore the draft to the profile revision captured when the editor opened or last successfully saved. |
| Cancel | Discard draft and proposal. If dirty, require confirmation. Restore summary and any draft-derived preview. |
| Save Profile | Validate, detect revision conflict, atomically persist, increment revision, invalidate profile caches, refresh summary, and record audit. |

## **21.3 Unknown-field preservation**

Profile Editor must not silently discard profile keys it does not expose. Two acceptable strategies are: use the complete typed current profile model with an extension map; or patch a validated JSON tree at known field paths while retaining all unmodified nodes. A deserialize-edit-reserialize path that loses future/mod-specific keys is rejected.

## **21.4 Canonicalization**

Canonical comparisons must normalize only semantically equivalent representations defined by the domain. The inventory hydration incident in which legacy metadata "{}" and runtime null compared unequal is a concrete warning: canonicalize both sides before equality, and restore pre-operation state if validation fails after mutation. Do not generalize this into aggressive normalization that changes meaningful profile text or JSON.

## **21.5 Length and content constraints**

* Define field-specific length budgets suitable for prompt containment and UI readability.  
* Reject control characters, invalid Unicode sequences, and malformed stable-ID references.  
* Do not strip creator punctuation or style merely to make generated output easier.  
* Separate player-facing biography from developer notes that should never enter normal prompts.  
* Preserve provenance indicating human-authored, generated-and-reviewed, migrated, or imported content.

## **21.6 Atomic save**

48. Revalidate active session, writer lease, stable NPC ID, and current base revision/hash.  
49. Build the complete canonical profile candidate with preserved extensions.  
50. Run schema and semantic validators.  
51. Write to a temporary sibling file.  
52. Flush/close and reread/validate the temporary file.  
53. Create or retain rollback copy according to repository policy.  
54. Atomically replace the authoritative profile file.  
55. Increment revision and write audit record.  
56. Invalidate/rebuild profile, prompt, and NPC self-model caches through existing owners.  
57. Refresh Profile Summary and reject any late result from the prior revision.

# **22\. Profile Generation Service**

NpcProfileGenerationService is a provider-neutral authoring assistant. Its visible action is Generate. It may use the current Orbis model/provider or a future approved authoring provider, but the UI must not expose the implementation model name or make generated prose authoritative.

![Profile generation provenance diagram from creator draft through proposal review and Save Profile to authored canon.][image9]

**Figure 9\. Generated profile content remains a proposal until explicit human review and Save Profile promote it into authored canon.**

## **22.1 Generation request**

record ProfileGenerationRequest(  
    UUID requestId,  
    UUID sessionId,  
    UUID npcStableId,  
    long pageGeneration,  
    long editorGeneration,  
    long baseProfileRevision,  
    String draftHash,  
    GenerationScope scope,  
    NpcProfileEditableFields currentDraft,  
    Optional\<WorldLorePacket\> approvedLore,  
    Map\<ProfileFieldPath, Integer\> fieldBudgets,  
    String schemaVersion  
) {}

## **22.2 Generation scopes**

* Biography only.  
* Personality and values.  
* Motivations and goals.  
* Speech style and mannerisms.  
* Fill missing allowed fields.  
* Refine selected text without altering facts.

The request should include creator facts and only approved, bounded lore relevant to the task. It should not include broad world state, private player memory, unrelated NPC records, credentials, raw logs, or hidden reasoning.

## **22.3 Structured output**

record GeneratedProfilePatch(  
    UUID requestId,  
    UUID npcStableId,  
    long baseProfileRevision,  
    String sourceDraftHash,  
    Map\<ProfileFieldPath, ProposedValue\> allowedChanges,  
    List\<GenerationWarning\> warnings,  
    ProviderGenerationMetadata metadata,  
    String schemaVersion  
) {}

* The allowlist excludes stable identity, file paths, inventory, gear, live relationships, memory, tasks, schedules, and world-state fields.  
* The output must be schema-validated before presentation.  
* Malformed, over-budget, or disallowed changes are rejected or quarantined, not partially applied invisibly.  
* Do not persist model chain-of-thought. Retain final proposed values, structured warnings, request identity, and provider metadata needed for audit.

## **22.4 Resource and lifecycle behavior**

* Run asynchronously through the existing Orbis resource scheduler with lower priority than active conversation and Hytale-critical work.  
* Apply timeout, cancellation, bounded retry, and output budget.  
* Cancel on editor close, session close, NPC deletion, provider shutdown, or a newer Generate request.  
* Accept output only when session, NPC, editor generation, base revision, and draft hash still match.  
* A provider failure degrades Generate only; manual profile editing remains available.

## **22.5 Proposal application**

Present a field-level diff. The creator may accept all, accept selected fields, edit proposed text, or discard. A proposal should not overwrite dirty manual fields without an explicit conflict decision. Accepted proposal values become ordinary draft values with provenance, not canon.

## **22.6 Generation quality checks**

| Check | Rule |
| :---- | :---- |
| Fact preservation | Do not contradict creator-supplied identity, relationships, dates, role, or approved lore |
| No invented current state | Do not claim present possessions, location, tasks, injuries, or relationships unless explicitly authored |
| No system leakage | Reject prompt text, implementation notes, model identity, or JSON instructions in prose fields |
| Field scope | Only requested/allowed fields may change |
| Length | Each proposed value stays within field budget |
| Tone | May be creative, but must remain compatible with current profile facts and intended setting |
| Safety | No executable commands, paths, credentials, or hidden control directives |

# **23\. Generated Content Provenance and Canon Promotion**

Generated authoring assistance intersects Orbis epistemics. The key rule is that a generated proposal is neither NPC memory nor evidence about the world. It becomes authored canon only through the same explicit profile save and ingestion path as manually authored content.

## **23.1 Provenance states**

| State | Meaning | May enter Orbis prompt/canon? |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| HUMAN\_DRAFT | Unsaved manual edit | No |
| GENERATED\_PROPOSAL | Unreviewed model output | No |
| GENERATED\_ACCEPTED\_DRAFT | Creator accepted/edited proposal in draft | No |
| AUTHORED\_CANON\_HUMAN | Human-authored value saved successfully | Yes, through normal profile ingestion |
| AUTHORED\_CANON\_GENERATED\_REVIEWED | Generated value reviewed and explicitly saved | Yes, marked with provenance |
| MIGRATED\_CANON | Existing data transformed by schema migration | Yes, with migration identity |

## **23.2 Forbidden propagation**

* Generate cannot write the belief store.  
* Generate cannot create episodic memories.  
* Generate cannot modify current relationships or reputation.  
* Generate cannot create tasks, schedules, inventory, or action results.  
* Generate cannot commit speech into CanonicalSpeechLedger.  
* Generate cannot cause the NPC to claim the proposal was experienced or remembered.

## **23.3 Canon ingestion**

58. Save Profile atomically commits the profile.  
59. Profile repository emits or exposes the new revision.  
60. Existing profile-to-self-model/canon ingestion validates the saved fields.  
61. Prompt and profile caches are invalidated.  
62. Future dialogue receives only the saved canonical version.  
63. Evaluation fixtures may record the change, but the act of generation itself is not testimony or experience.

## **23.4 Audit record**

record GeneratedCanonProvenance(  
    UUID proposalId,  
    String providerId,  
    String providerModel,  
    String sourceDraftHash,  
    Set\<ProfileFieldPath\> acceptedFields,  
    UUID acceptingPlayerId,  
    Instant acceptedAt,  
    long committedProfileRevision  
) {}

Store only the provenance needed to explain how saved text was produced. Do not retain hidden reasoning, unnecessary prompts containing private data, or credentials.

# **24\. Appearance Editor Feasibility and API Boundary**

The recommended approach is a custom server-driven NPC Appearance Editor inspired by Hytale's My Avatar experience, backed by Hytale's cosmetics data and PlayerSkin representation. Do not attempt to make the native My Avatar controller edit a non-player target unless a future supported API explicitly permits it.

The current protocol PlayerSkin carries body characteristic, underwear, face, eyes, ears, mouth, facial hair, haircut, eyebrows, pants, overpants, undertop, overtop, shoes, head accessory, face accessory, ear accessory, skin feature, gloves, and cape fields. \[H7\] Community Wardrobe demonstrates that a familiar server-driven cosmetic customization experience is feasible, but its AGPL implementation is reference-only unless license review approves reuse. \[C1\]

## **24.1 Feasibility decision**

| Approach | Status | Decision |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Invoke native My Avatar page against NPC | No supported server contract proven | Do not base implementation on it |
| Custom UI with Hytale cosmetics catalog | Strongly feasible, exact APIs version-sensitive | Recommended |
| Invent new appearance schema | Unnecessary and incompatible risk | Reject |
| Edit logged-in player's avatar then export | Current manual workaround only | Replace with NPC-targeted save |
| Copy community Wardrobe code | License-dependent | Reference architecture only unless approved |

## **24.2 Server API preflight**

* Enumerate the exact current CosmeticRegistry API and catalog fields.  
* Confirm the server-side skin parse/validation/model-creation functions in the installed build.  
* Confirm the existing ImmersiveNPCs skin JSON format and adapter path.  
* Confirm CharacterPreviewComponent supports repeated draft updates without mutating the Player.  
* Confirm color/gradient/variant information exposed for each cosmetic category.  
* Record Hytale build identity and fail closed if a future build changes required codecs or category semantics.

## **24.3 No player-avatar mutation**

The appearance editor targets an NPC-owned draft and saved skin. The player's own skin is used only as the viewer context required by the preview protocol, if necessary. Every open, update, cancel, close, disconnect, and exception path must restore the viewer's original skin/model/equipment state exactly.

# **25\. Cosmetics Catalog Service**

NpcAppearanceCatalogService exposes a stable, searchable, paginated view of the current Hytale cosmetic registry. It is a read-only catalog service, not an appearance persistence owner.

## **25.1 Catalog snapshot identity**

record CosmeticCatalogIdentity(  
    String hytaleBuildId,  
    String registryRevisionOrHash,  
    String enabledAssetPackSetHash,  
    String schemaVersion  
) {}

## **25.2 Catalog entry**

record CosmeticOptionDescriptor(  
    CosmeticCategory category,  
    String cosmeticId,  
    String displayName,  
    Optional\<String\> iconAsset,  
    List\<CosmeticVariantDescriptor\> variants,  
    List\<ColorChoice\> colors,  
    Set\<CosmeticCategory\> hiddenOrConflictingSlots,  
    CompatibilityMetadata compatibility,  
    String sourceAssetPack  
) {}

## **25.3 Category mapping**

| Primary rail | Secondary categories |
| :---- | :---- |
| Body | Body Characteristic, Underwear, Skin Feature |
| Face | Face, Mouth, Ears, Eyebrows, Facial Hair |
| Hair | Haircut and any hair-specific variants |
| Eyes | Eyes and eye color/gradient options |
| Clothing | Undertop, Overtop, Pants, Overpants, Shoes, Gloves |
| Accessories | Head, Face, Ear accessories, Cape |

## **25.4 Loading and cache policy**

* Build or refresh catalog off the world/UI callback when API safety allows.  
* Cache immutable descriptors by catalog identity.  
* Do not send the full catalog in one page update.  
* Load one selected category and one page of options at a time.  
* Debounce search and cancel stale query results.  
* Invalidate catalog when enabled asset packs or Hytale build identity changes.  
* Do not persist local developer file paths in descriptors.

## **25.5 Search**
